title: Fix Find-FreeSubnets hanging indefinitely with multiple VNet address spaces
body:
`Find-FreeSubnets` hangs when a VNet has multiple address spaces (e.g. a private `10.0.0.0/16` alongside a globally-routable range like `203.0.113.0/24`).

## Root cause

For each address space iteration, the sorted subnet list was built from **all** subnets across all address spaces. IPs above `128.0.0.0` produce **negative** signed `Int32` values, so globally-routable subnets sort *before* the fake-before sentinel. This manufactures a spurious gap of ~132 million addresses, driving the inner CIDR enumeration `for` loop into ~16 million iterations.

## Fix

- **`VNet.psm1`** — Before building the sorted list, filter `$vnet.Subnets.AddressPrefix` to only subnets whose start IP falls within the current address space bounds. Signed-integer comparisons are safe here: a cross-space subnet always fails at least one of the `-ge`/`-le` bounds because positive and negative `Int32` ranges never overlap for the address spaces in question. A `$null` guard handles the empty-`Subnets` edge case.

```powershell
$vnetRangeStart = [Net.IPAddress]::NetworkToHostOrder([BitConverter]::ToInt32($vnetStart.GetAddressBytes(), 0))
$vnetRangeEnd   = [Net.IPAddress]::NetworkToHostOrder([BitConverter]::ToInt32($vnetEnd.GetAddressBytes(), 0))

$subnetsInAddressSpace = $vnet.Subnets.AddressPrefix | Where-Object {
    if ($null -eq $_) { return $false }
    $subnetStart, $null = cidrToIpRange $_
    $subnetStartNum = [Net.IPAddress]::NetworkToHostOrder([BitConverter]::ToInt32($subnetStart.GetAddressBytes(), 0))
    $subnetStartNum -ge $vnetRangeStart -and $subnetStartNum -le $vnetRangeEnd
}

$sorted = @($beforeFirstAvailableCidr) + @($subnetsInAddressSpace) + @($afterLastAvailableCidr) | Sort-Object ...
```

- **`VNet.Tests.ps1` + `Find-FreeSubnets-MultipleAddressSpaces.Expected.json`** — Regression test using a VNet with `10.0.0.0/24` (private) and `203.0.113.0/24` (globally-routable), directly matching the reported configuration.
